title: Test-Driven Development (TDD) for AI Systems
description: Adapt Test-Driven Development (Red-Green-Refactor) for probabilistic AI: testing deterministic boundaries, tool contracts, and regression suites.

data.text: Can You Practice TDD with Probabilistic Models?

A frequent objection among developers is: 'You cannot do Test-Driven Development with LLMs because model responses are non-deterministic and change constantly.' This is a misconception. In modern AI engineering, over 80% of an AI feature consists of deterministic software: prompt template construction, input boundary validation, JSON Schema derivation, tool argument parsing, database mutation guards, and error recovery policies. TDD is not only possible for AI—it is essential.
The Two-Tier TDD Cycle for AI Systems

rows: Prompt assembly, tool schema generation, response parsing, validation logic
On every code change (sub-second local runs)
Model accuracy, factual grounding, retrieval recall against golden dataset
Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation against live model with fixed Seed
Automated in CI/CD on pull requests and nightly builds

data.text: Step-by-Step TDD Example: Writing a Strict JSON Schema Parser

Following the classic TDD workflow: 1. Red: Write a failing test asserting that malformed or out-of-range AI outputs throw meaningful validation exceptions. 2. Green: Implement the minimal C# parser code to pass the test. 3. Refactor: Optimize performance and error logging.

data.title: TDD Unit Test for AI Tool Parameter Validator in C#
data.content: Writing the test first to specify the contract for AI argument validation:

data.text: Whenever you expose a C# method as an AI tool, write a contract test verifying that AIFunctionFactory.Create produces the expected JSON Schema (property names, descriptions, required attributes) so you catch breaking schema changes before deploying to production.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Practice TDD on the deterministic 80% of your AI codebase: prompts, schemas, parsers, and guardrails
Separate fast, deterministic unit test TDD from asynchronous probabilistic evaluation benchmarks
Write tests first to define the validation contract for tool arguments generated by LLMs
Contract test tool schemas to guarantee that C# refactors don't silently alter tool parameters
Combine Red-Green-Refactor with CI evaluation gates to ensure regressions are caught early
data.takeaway: TDD brings architectural discipline to AI engineering. Testing the deterministic boundaries first shields your application against the inherent volatility of probabilistic models.
